one_liner: Estimates each number's own chance of being drawn from all earlier draws of the current era, counted equally, starting from the fair-draw chance.
registry_status_reason: Released by package REL-1 (releases and WF-1 design v0.1r1, owner decisions WF1-1 and WF1-2, ratified 31 October 2026). Contract runs on real data need the separate real-development gate.
short_explanation: E_6 treats each number on its own. For every earlier draw it notes whether the number was drawn, and estimates the number's chance with the standard Beta-Bernoulli model: it starts from the fair-draw chance (7 in 47 for a main number), worth one draw of evidence, and updates it with the history. Every earlier draw counts equally, so it ranks the numbers in the same order as E_1's counts; only the order of numbers with exactly equal counts can differ, because the tie rule includes the method and variant. The estimated chances are the scores: its top pick is the highest-ranked numbers and its inverse pick the lowest-ranked, with exact ties settled by the project tie rule (TIE_SHA256_V1). The chances are also published as probabilities, labelled as uncalibrated model outputs, because the model ignores that the main numbers are drawn together. It uses only which numbers were drawn, not their order or the dates. If the draws are fair, it is not expected to beat chance.
